data.one_liner: JavaScript engine for Flutter using QuickJS and JavaScriptCore via FFI.
data.what_it_does: Provides a unified JavaScript runtime across Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux using native engines (QuickJS and JavaScriptCore). Allows evaluating JavaScript code, handling promises, and executing HTTP requests (xhr/fetch) synchronously through Dart FFI.
use_when: You need to run JavaScript libraries natively within your Flutter app without a hidden WebView
You want to share business logic, validation rules, or scripts between your web app and mobile/desktop apps
You need to evaluate JavaScript and communicate between Dart and JS via channels
avoid_when: You require a full browser DOM environment (consider WebView alternatives instead)
You want to avoid native engine dependencies or binary size increases
strengths: Unified API for QuickJS and JavaScriptCore across multiple platforms
Supports fetch, xhr, and promises out of the box
Small APK footprint compared to V8-based alternatives
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific configuration for release builds (such as Proguard rules on Android or entitlements on macOS)
Debugging JavaScript on certain platforms requires specific configuration
data.setup_notes: Requires changing the minimum Android SDK version to 21 and setting up Proguard rules for Android release builds. macOS requires entitlements for network and JIT access if making HTTP calls.
